channel.title: Crypto Readout
channel.description: Crypto Readout reports on Bitcoin, Ethereum and altcoin markets, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, network upgrades and crypto regulation worldwide.

item.title: Buying Chain-Specific Coverage With XMR
item.description: Chain-specific cover follows the network or protocol named in its policy; paying in XMR is a separate step that depends on the provider’s payment rails.

item.title: How Cross-Chain Tax Recording Follows Your Crypto
item.description: Cross-chain tax records connect transactions across networks, preserve cost basis through transfers, and flag bridge fees or swaps that may count as disposals.

item.title: Why Polygon PoS Withdrawals Wait for a Checkpoint
item.description: A Polygon PoS withdrawal waits for a checkpoint to include its burn on Ethereum, then needs a separate claim transaction before the asset is released.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional self-custody for crypto advisers
item.description: The SEC has proposed a custody framework for advisers and funds that allows conditional self-custody and state trust companies, with safeguards for keys and client assets.

item.title: September crypto hacks topped $766 million, led by Bitget and Liquid
item.description: PeckShield and CertiK put September crypto thefts above $766 million, led by Bitget and Liquid Network, though much of Liquid’s bitcoin was returned.

item.title: How to Choose a Blackhole Swap Pool for Trades and Liquidity
item.description: A swap pool prices trades from token reserves, so compare depth, price impact and LP risk before choosing where to trade or add liquidity on Avalanche.

item.title: Bungee Bridge: From Approval to Destination
item.description: A bungee bridge transfer is a route across chains, not a single coin teleport: the source transaction, route and destination settlement each shape when funds arrive.

item.title: How TRON Shares Energy Between Wallets
item.description: TRON lets one account lend staked Energy to another address, so that address can run contract calls; the stake stays with its owner and fees can still apply.

item.title: How to rent TRON energy for a USDT transfer
item.description: Renting TRON energy lets a provider delegate execution capacity to your wallet, so a USDT transfer can use that resource instead of burning as much TRX.

item.title: How to convert XMR to USDT after a trading loss
item.description: To turn XMR into USDT after a loss, choose a supported route, check the quote and destination network, then verify settlement before moving or spending funds.

item.title: Set an XMR Bridge Minimum After Rounding
item.description: A bridge should compare its payout floor with the amount left after fees and destination-unit rounding, so a valid quote cannot become an undersized transfer.

item.title: Why Early Swaps Move Prices in Crypto Launch Pools
item.description: A launch pool's opening price depends on its rules and starting liquidity; early buys and sells change reserves, execution prices and later quotes.

item.title: How to Choose a Stablecoin Pool
item.description: A stablecoin pool trades off token quality, pool balance, exit costs and contract risk; compare each before depositing, rather than choosing by quoted yield.

item.title: Three Checks Before an Avalanche Token Swap
item.description: Before swapping Avalanche tokens, verify the network and token, compare the quoted output with fees, and set a minimum amount that protects against price movement.

item.title: How to Verify a Token Contract Address Before a Swap
item.description: A ticker can be copied, but a contract address identifies a token on one chain; verify it from the project’s official source before approving a swap.

item.title: Why a token permit signature fails
item.description: A permit fails when its signed fields, nonce, deadline or token domain do not match the contract’s checks; compare those inputs before signing again on the same chain.

item.title: Four Checks for Pool Depth Before a Thin Token Swap
item.description: A thin token’s pool can look deep until a trade moves its price; check active liquidity, quote impact, reserves and route before approving a swap.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Timeout Can End Before Your Funds Return
item.description: Cross-chain timeout windows depend on the route’s contracts and settlement rules; a transfer can stop waiting before a refund or recovery is complete.

item.title: Why a Test Transfer Finds Cross-Chain Mistakes
item.description: A small test transfer checks the route, destination and wallet setup before a larger cross-chain move, while showing which risks it cannot rule out on its own.

item.title: Set a Minimum for a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A minimum output sets the least you will accept after a cross-chain swap; learn how it affects execution, refunds and the amount you should enter.
